papers.title: Who Remembers What? Multi-Granularity Memory Extraction for Multi-User, Multi-Agent Interaction
papers.problem: AI agents that share lessons across many users risk leaking one person's private facts to others.
papers.fix: MixUA scopes each lesson, lifts pass rates by up to 16 points, and leaks at most 0.02% of private probes.
papers.practicalUseCase: Shared agent memory can help everyone without exposing secrets, so scope each stored lesson to the people it benefits.
papers.limitation: The tests used five users and seven agents, so results at larger scale are unknown.

papers.title: EgoX: Egocentric Cross-Embodiment Manipulation with Embodiment Dreaming
papers.problem: Robots struggle to learn from human, robot, and simulated demonstrations together because their bodies and controls differ.
papers.fix: Mixed pretraining raised average task progress from 0.63 to 0.80, and from 0.53 to 0.77 in unfamiliar conditions.
papers.practicalUseCase: Mixed data from different bodies helps robots in new conditions, so pool data instead of training from scratch.
papers.limitation: The tests covered five tasks and six robot bodies, so other robots may behave differently.

papers.title: Back to Pixels: Lifting Latent Video Diffusion into Pixel Space
papers.problem: Video generators that work in compressed space limit high resolution, per-frame control, and fast response to each action.
papers.fix: PixVid draws every frame in pixels, matches the baseline, and doubles resolution at the same per-frame token count.
papers.practicalUseCase: Pixel-space video lets editing tools react at the next frame, so interactive video tools become practical.
papers.limitation: It matches the baseline only after fine-tuning one model, Wan2.1-14B, on about 1.3M clips.

papers.title: Consensus Capture in Reference-Based UAV Video Stabilization: A Benchmark on Dynamic Urban Scenes
papers.problem: Drone stabilizers are tested where only the camera moves, but moving cars on busy roads pull the estimate off.
papers.fix: Unmasked ORB followed moving cars on 28 of 304 real-time pairs, with 18.8 pixels median error; masking fixed every method.
papers.practicalUseCase: Normal quality checks miss this failure, so mask moving objects before aligning drone footage of traffic.
papers.limitation: The tests used drone footage over one busy intersection type, so other scenes may differ.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Nobody knew how sustainability sukuk issuance grew or what makes an issue large.
papers.fix: Among 11,944 sukuk issues from 2012 to 2022, sustainability sukuk stay tiny and cluster in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia.
papers.practicalUseCase: Larger issues come from equity-based contracts, strong security, and major currencies, so issuers should design deals around those features.
papers.limitation: The data stops at 2022 and shows links between features and size, not cause.

papers.title: Islamic Social Financial Instruments and Sustainable Community Development: Evidence Synthesis on Community Resilience
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Research on zakat, waqf, and sadaqah is scattered, so nobody had a clear picture of how they build community resilience.
papers.fix: Across 93 studies, zakat gives short-term relief, waqf builds long-term assets, and sadaqah covers flexible emergency needs.
papers.practicalUseCase: Combined ZISWAF models work best, so communities should pair the three tools under strong governance.
papers.limitation: It reviews published studies, so it inherits their gaps and cannot prove cause.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks create sustainability committees, but nobody knew whether they change real environmental work at Islamic banks.
papers.fix: Committees lift all four environmental scores at conventional banks, but only two scores at Islamic banks.
papers.practicalUseCase: Committee effects at Islamic banks look mostly symbolic, so regulators should check for real products and innovations.
papers.limitation: It shows links in bank data, not proof that committees cause the changes.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked evidence on whether AI and big data actually improve their competitiveness and sustainability.
papers.fix: A survey of 214 managers found AI, data analytics, and data management all link positively to competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital investment pays off for competitiveness, so invest in AI and data practices, not only staff skills.
papers.limitation: The survey covers one country and one moment, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: It was unclear which digital and institutional factors drive growth in banks that run both Islamic and conventional systems.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT is the strongest growth driver, and high-tech exports help only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Digital tools drive bank growth, so banks and regulators should fund digital infrastructure together with national innovation.
papers.limitation: The data covers 12 countries and shows statistical links, so other markets may differ.

papers.title: Procrastination among US college students: Prevalence and impact relative to common health and life issues
papers.problem: Nobody knew how common student procrastination is, or how its harm compares with other health and life problems.
papers.fix: Among 65,950 US students, 72.3% reported procrastination, and 45.4% said it hurt their grades, far more than finances or ADHD.
papers.practicalUseCase: Procrastination hurts more students than most other problems, so treat it as a main target for study support.
papers.limitation: It relies on student self-reports from US colleges, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: “The significance of context”: Fit, friction, and function in the work lives of early career academics with ADHD
papers.problem: Little data showed how early-career academics with ADHD experience building a research career.
papers.fix: Interviews show academia can reward ADHD traits, but social and institutional pressure often blocks that potential.
papers.practicalUseCase: Workplace fit matters, so universities should adjust the environment instead of treating ADHD only as a medical problem.
papers.limitation: It is an interview study of early-career academics, so it cannot show how common these experiences are.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant tests and comparison, which may make them feel like frauds, but the global scale was unclear.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings are common among pre-licensure medical students worldwide, though results vary by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: Many medical students likely feel like frauds, so schools should measure it the same way and test support programs.
papers.limitation: Results differed a lot between studies, so the pooled estimate needs careful reading.
